```{r,echo=FALSE}
# sqrt(x)/a = b

while(T){
    sab = sample(c(-1,1),1)
    a = sample(2:6,1)*sab
    b = sample(2:6,1)*sab
    sqrtx = a*b
    x = (a*b)^2
    if(sqrtx<17){break}
}

eq = paste0("\\frac{\\sqrt{x}}{",a,"}=",b)
eq2 = paste0("\\sqrt{x}=",a*b)

eq3 = paste0("\\frac{\\sqrt{",x,"}}{",a,"}\\stackrel{?}{=}",b)

eq4 = paste0("\\frac{",sqrtx,"}{",a,"}\\stackrel{?}{=}",b)

```

Question
========

Solve.

$$`r eq`$$

Solution
========

Multiply both sides by `r a`.


$$`r eq2`$$

Square both sides.

$$x=`r x`$$

Check the solution in the original equation.

$$`r eq3`$$

$$`r eq4`$$

Yup, that is true. So $x=`r x`$ is a solution to the given equation.
